title: Odile and the Will
premise: Retired detective Yara Vane has spent five years hiding in her failing bookshop, cataloging the town of Marrow Bay's secrets instead of her own grief. When a stranger leaves a diary belonging to Odile Marchetti—the girl who vanished five years ago and whose case was closed with a man's conviction—Yara discovers entries written after the disappearance, proving Odile was alive and someone in town knows it. Pulled back into the case by the victim's sister and a corrupt sheriff racing to start a wrongful trial, Yara uncovers a cover-up implicating the town's founding families. In the end, Yara exposes the truth at the courthouse, Odile returns alive to testify against the man who hid her, and Yara finally claims the found family she'd been too afraid to keep.
about_author: Sebastian Nakamura is a former small-town court clerk who spent a decade transcribing testimonies that never quite added up. He writes mysteries from a converted boathouse on the Pacific coast, where he still keeps his first case file pinned above his desk.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: Yara Vane's POV. In her failing bookshop, Yara files an anonymous letter among her private archive of Marrow Bay's secrets, refusing to open it. We learn she left the detective bureau five years ago after the Odile Marchetti case closed. Emotional beat: the comfort of order cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: A Diary That Keeps Writing
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A nervous young man, Theo Marchetti, begs Yara to look at his missing sister's diary, recovered from a riverbank. The final entry is dated three weeks after Odile vanished. Yara recognizes the handwriting as genuine. Emotional beat: dread—the closed case opening like a wound.

chapters.title: What the Sheriff Promised
chapters.summary: Sheriff Dale Pruitt's POV. Pruitt, up for re-election, prepares to charge local handyman Roy Calloway in a retrial, pressured by the influential Aldous family. He learns the diary exists and orders it seized. Emotional beat: a man rehearsing a lie until it feels like memory.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Filed Everything
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara studies the diary against her old case notes and finds a detail no forger would know: Odile's habit of encoding dates as book titles. One coded entry points to the old cannery. Emotional beat: the detective waking up after five years of sleep.

chapters.title: Theo
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confesses he waited five years to bring Yara the diary because their mother forbade it; now their mother is dead and the retrial looms. He needs Yara to prove Roy Calloway innocent before the trial begins. Emotional beat: grief handing its burden to a stranger.

chapters.title: The Cannery at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the condemned cannery, Yara finds a hidden room: blankets, canned food, a child's drawing signed 'O'. Someone lived here—recently. She's watched from the tree line by an unseen figure. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Roy Calloway, In His Cell
chapters.summary: Roy's POV. Imprisoned and abandoned, Roy insists he never touched Odile—he drove her to the bus station the night she ran, paid for by someone whose face he never saw. Yara visits; he begs her to believe him. Emotional beat: dignity surviving in a small, dirty room.

chapters.title: The Aldous Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Digging into the founding family, Yara finds the Aldous estate paid Roy's legal fees—control dressed as charity—and that Odile's mother once worked for them. The diary is confiscated by Pruitt's deputy. Emotional beat: the shape of a conspiracy becoming visible.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading Over My Shoulder
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara's bookshop is ransacked; her private archive of town secrets is gone. Only the diary pages she hid survive. She realizes the archive was the real target. Emotional beat: fear, then fury—the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Librarian's Debt
chapters.summary: Marge, the town librarian, POV. Marge admits to Yara that Aldous money saved the library, and in exchange she reported 'odd inquiries' to the family for years—including Yara's. Emotional beat: complicity and shame in a woman who thought she was neutral.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Decoding more entries, Yara finds Odile wrote about 'the man with the boat shoes' watching her, and a plan: 'If I go, look where the herons nest.' The diary's later entries are in a different hand—or a changed one. Emotional beat: Odile becoming a person, not a file.

chapters.title: Where the Herons Nest
chapters.summary: Yara and Theo's POV, alternating. At the marsh, they find a weatherproof cache: cash, a burner phone, and a note in Odile's hand—'Don't trust the sheriff. Don't trust the family. Trust no one with a badge.' Emotional beat: the missing girl orchestrating her own survival from the past.

chapters.title: Pruitt's War
chapters.summary: Sheriff Pruitt's POV. Pruitt learns Yara visited Roy and searched the marsh; he threatens her with obstruction charges. Privately, he calls Aldous's lawyer, who tells him to let the trial start fast. Emotional beat: a weak man realizing he's the expendable part.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Vigil
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Neighbors quietly rally: Marge brings coffee, the diner owner leaves food, teenagers sweep the broken glass. For the first time, Yara sees she has a town, not just an archive of it. Emotional beat: found family arriving unannounced.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Ferry Photo
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A tourist's ferry photo from two years ago shows a woman resembling adult Odile. Yara traces the ferry route to a coastal village. Emotional beat: the impossible becoming a lead.

chapters.title: Roy's Trial Date Is Set
chapters.summary: Roy's POV. The retrial is scheduled in three weeks. Roy's new court-appointed lawyer is competent but terrified of the Aldous name. Roy tells Yara: 'You're the only one still digging.' Emotional beat: a condemned man's faith, heavier than any verdict.

chapters.title: The Mother's Letters
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds his late mother's hidden letters to Odile—she knew Odile was alive and mailed her money through the ferry office, sworn to silence by an Aldous man who visited after the disappearance. Emotional beat: a mother's terrible bargain.

chapters.title: What Odile Saw
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Reassembling the timeline, Yara deduces Odile witnessed something at the Aldous estate the night she vanished—likely involving the family patriarch's death being staged as natural. Her 'disappearance' was partly flight, partly arranged hiding. Emotional beat: the case inverting—victim into witness.

chapters.title: A Visit from Mr. Voss
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The Aldous family's lawyer, Voss, offers Yara money to hand over the diary and forget the ferry lead. He mentions her late partner's name, a threat wrapped in courtesy. Emotional beat: cold fear, and Yara refusing it.

chapters.title: The Ferry Office Records
chapters.summary: Yara and Marge's POV. Marge uses library credentials to pull ferry office records: monthly money orders to 'E. Marsh,' signed in Odile's hand, ending eight months ago. Emotional beat: the trail going cold just as it warms—panic.

chapters.title: Eight Months of Silence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo spirals: did Odile die after all? Yara steadies him, sharing her own story—why she left the bureau, the case she couldn't close, the partner she lost. Emotional beat: two broken people building something like trust.

chapters.title: The Deputy Who Flinched
chapters.summary: Deputy Cora Lin's POV. Cora, Pruitt's deputy, was ordered to burn the confiscated diary but kept it. She brings it to Yara, confessing she joined the force to be the cop her town never had. Emotional beat: a conscience defecting.

chapters.title: The Second Diary
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The recovered diary contains entries Yara hadn't seen: Odile describing her hidden life, her fear of 'the man who found me once,' and a promise to return 'when the old man's will is read.' Emotional beat: understanding—Odile was waiting for an inheritance to force her home.

chapters.title: The Will
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara discovers patriarch Edmund Aldous amended his will weeks before his death, leaving a contingent bequest to 'the girl from the boathouse'—Odile. The family buried the amendment. The title clicks: Odile and the will. Emotional beat: the motive finally standing upright.

chapters.title: Voss's Mistake
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss realizes Yara has the will's trail and panics, ordering the boathouse where Odile once hid searched—and a tail put on Yara. Emotional beat: the hunter becoming visible to himself.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Marsh
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Following a staged clue, Yara is ambushed by Voss's fixer; she escapes into the marsh with a wounded shoulder, saved by Cora, who was tailing her and chose her side. Emotional beat: terror, then the fierce relief of an ally.

chapters.title: E. Marsh
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. 'E. Marsh' isn't just a pun on the heron marsh—Yara finds a rented cabin under that name, recently paid by money order. Inside: signs of hurried departure and a fresh note: 'If you're reading this, you're the detective from the books. I need you.' Emotional beat: the missing girl asking for help at last.

chapters.title: Cora's Report
chapters.summary: Deputy Cora's POV. Cora files a formal report on the diary suppression and the ambush, knowing it ends her career. Pruitt, cornered, reveals Voss pressured him from the start—but claims he doesn't know where Odile is. Emotional beat: a badge returned to its meaning.

chapters.title: The Trial Begins
chapters.summary: Roy's POV. Roy's retrial opens with the prosecution painting him as a predator. Yara sits in the gallery with Theo and Marge, holding evidence she can't yet legally enter. Emotional beat: the machinery of injustice grinding in daylight.

chapters.title: A Witness in the Gallery
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara tracks the fixer to a marina and finds proof he searched for Odile on the family's payroll five years ago. But Voss moves first, getting Yara barred from the courthouse as a 'harasser.' Emotional beat: the walls closing in.

chapters.title: What the Herons Knew
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Re-reading Odile's coded entries one final time, Yara realizes 'where the herons nest' also names the Aldous estate's boathouse—Odile never left the region at first; she was hidden, then fled the hider. Emotional beat: the last lock clicking open.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Yara and Cora's POV. At the estate boathouse, they find the fixer waiting—and Odile Marchetti, alive, having returned secretly to steal the will amendment herself. She's been running from Voss's fixer for eight months. Emotional beat: a ghost made flesh, armed and exhausted.

chapters.title: Odile's Testimony
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile tells her story: she saw Voss and the family patriarch's heir stage the death, ran, was found and hidden by a family retainer who grew afraid, then escaped. She trusts Yara because the diary chose her. Emotional beat: five years of silence ending in one breath.

chapters.title: Getting Her to the Courthouse
chapters.summary: Yara, Cora, and Theo's POV, braided. The team smuggles Odile past the fixer and Voss's watchers to the courthouse as Roy's defense rests. Emotional beat: a found family executing its first mission together.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Well of the Court
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile walks into the courtroom; the room stops. She testifies to what she saw and why she ran. The judge orders the will amendment entered into evidence. Emotional beat: catharsis—the truth spoken aloud where it was buried.

chapters.title: Pruitt Breaks
chapters.summary: Sheriff Pruitt's POV. Confronted with Cora's report and Odile's testimony, Pruitt confesses his role in suppressing the diary, implicating Voss and the heir. Emotional beat: a coward's redemption, bought too late to be clean but in time to matter.

chapters.title: The Verdict
chapters.summary: Roy's POV. The jury acquits Roy in under two hours; Voss and the heir are arrested. Roy walks free into a town that finally says his name kindly. Emotional beat: justice arriving outside the law that failed him.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The amended will is honored: Odile receives the bequest and, with it, the standing to stay. She and Theo scatter their mother's letters into the heron marsh. Emotional beat: inheritance as permission to belong.

chapters.title: Shelves, Reshelved
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara reopens the bookshop with Cora as partner and Marge as unofficial archivist. She files the case closed—truly closed—and puts Odile's diary on a shelf labeled 'Returned.' Emotional beat: peace earned, not defaulted.

chapters.title: Odile and the Will
chapters.summary: Odile and Yara's POV, alternating. Weeks later, Odile visits the shop; Yara offers her a job and a key. Odile asks what Yara will do now. 'Whatever the town needs filed,' Yara says. Emotional beat: two women who survived being hidden, choosing to be found.
